paras: The attempted lynching of F. G. Polanski took place at Barnesville, Minnesota, on the night of Thursday, March 29, 1888, when armed men broke into the town jail and carried off Polanski, a hardware merchant held on his wife's complaint of assault. Armed officers and a posse of citizens rescued him before he was harmed, and the short dispatch describing the averted "lynching bee" ran in papers from Connecticut to Dakota Territory.

Polanski, described in one version as "a hardware merchant," had been arrested for assault on complaint of his wife and lodged in the Barnesville jail. The reports give no race for him or for the men who came for him, and they state no motive for the mob beyond the charge.

That night, according to the Minneapolis Journal's Barnesville correspondent, "a mob of armed men broke in and carried him off." The officers, aided by a posse of citizens, rescued the prisoner before he had been harmed. No one was reported killed or injured.
No report of arrests among the mob, or of what became of the assault charge, appears in the coverage.

The story reached the press as a special to the Minneapolis Journal, dated March 30, and was reprinted almost word for word. The Waterbury Evening Democrat and the Beatrice Daily Express carried it on March 31 under the headlines "Saved from Being Lynched" and "Lynching Bee." The Brookhaven Leader in Mississippi folded it into a column of "Additional Dispatches" on April 5, and the Custer Chronicle in Dakota Territory ran it under "Lynching" on April 7.

Each version credited "the interference of armed officers and citizens" for the outcome and offered no comment on the mob. The texts varied in small details: the Custer paper spelled the name "Pollinski" and wrote of "an armed man" while still referring to "the mob," and the Brookhaven digest gave his initials as "E. G." and the date as "the 30th."

reader.title: Attempted lynching of F. G. Polanski
bases: An armed mob broke into the Barnesville jail and carried off a prisoner in what the dispatch called a 'lynching bee' before officers and a posse rescued him (A1, A2, A4).

No one was killed: officers and a citizens' posse rescued the prisoner before the mob harmed him (A1, A2); the seizure of a man jailed on an assault charge was an attempted lynching, not a completed one.

All four reports of the Barnesville episode carry the same Minneapolis Journal special from Barnesville, reprinted with small variations (A1, A2, A3, A4); no independent local or follow-up report was found.
